key_insight: A geometry-aware state space model (SSM) treats a whole-slide image as a spatially-anchored sequence of patch embeddings, enabling efficient capture of long-range spatial interactions across thousands of tiles and replacing the traditional two-stage MIL pipeline with a unified geometry-aware aggregator.
problem_solved: Aggregating thousands of patch-level features in gigapixel whole-slide images while preserving spatial geometry and long-range dependencies—limitations of conventional two-stage Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) that often ignores explicit spatial relations and struggles with scalability.
method: Encode WSIs as sequences of patch embeddings augmented with explicit 2D spatial coordinates/geometry-aware positional encodings.
Use a state space model whose transition/update dynamics are modulated by geometric relationships to capture long-range, order-aware interactions among distant patches.
Perform efficient slide-level aggregation with the SSM (linear or near-linear complexity), enabling end-to-end training and scalable inference on gigapixel slides.
impact: Provides a scalable, geometry-aware alternative to MIL that improves representation of spatial context in computational pathology, enabling more accurate and interpretable slide-level predictions and practical training on large WSI datasets.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: WSI → tiled patches (with coordinates) → geometry-aware SSM aggregator → slide-level prediction

paper_title: Geometry-Aware State Space Model: A New Paradigm for Whole-Slide Image Representation
paper_authors: Enhui Chai, Sicheng Chen, Tianyi Zhang, Chad Wong, Kecheng Huang
